question: Within a tool family, do outlines from a middle period sit in between the earlier and later outlines in shape space (gradual change), stay with the earlier ones (change came later), already match the later ones (change came earlier), or lie off the way between them (a distinct middle form)?
note: Registered after the user proposed a 1750-1850 window and after only the per-period record counts had been inspected; no shape statistic had been computed. Descriptive and collection-bound: almost all dated outlines are from Museum Boerhaave, catalog dates are attributions, and a family mixes sub-types whose share changes over time, so a shift between periods can come from what was collected or catalogued rather than from design.
periods_rule: a record belongs to a period only if its whole catalog date range lies inside it: early = start >= early_from and end <= window start; middle = start >= window start and end <= window end; late = start >= window end and end <= 2025. Records straddling a boundary, undated records and earlier records are counted, not used.

statistics.axis: d = mean latent of late records minus mean latent of early records
statistics.position: t = mean over middle records of (z - mean_early) . d / |d|^2 (0 = like the early mean, 1 = like the late mean)
statistics.offset: distance of the middle mean from the early-late line, divided by |d|
statistics.uncertainty: 95% percentile intervals from 2000 bootstrap resamples of leakage groups within each period (seed 17), recomputing all means
statistics.change_exists: permutation test of |d|: shuffle early/late labels within the family 2000 times (seed 17); one-sided p
statistics.offset_null: shuffle early/middle/late labels within the family 2000 times (seed 18); share of shuffles with an offset at least as large

decision_rule: Per family and window. If the change test has p >= 0.05: 'no clear change to locate'. Otherwise: 'in between' if the 95% interval of t lies inside (0, 1); 'still like the early tools' if it contains 0; 'already like the late tools' if it contains 1; 'unclear' if it contains both. Separately, 'off the way' is flagged if the offset exceeds 95% of its shuffled values.
pictures_rule: the latent decoder (configs/ml/latent_decoder.json) draws the normalised early mean, the middle mean and the late mean, and 5 evenly spaced stops on the spherical path from the early to the late mean (one sample each, same starting noise, seed 17 + 900); display only
